name: Steven Spielberg
hook: The blockbuster auteur Jeopardy connects to Jaws, E.T., and a record run of John Williams scores.

facts.label: Night Gallery
facts.statement: A college dropout not yet 23, Spielberg directed one segment of Rod Serling's Night Gallery when it premiered in 1969.

facts.label: John Williams
facts.statement: John Williams has scored more than 25 Spielberg films since 1974, including Jaws, E.T., and Schindler's List.

facts.label: Jaws
facts.statement: Jaws (1975) named its mechanical shark Bruce after Spielberg's lawyer; Robert Shaw croons "Farewell and adieu, you fair Spanish ladies."

facts.label: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
facts.statement: Close Encounters of the Third Kind (1977) is his aliens-in-America film; Jack Nicholson turned it down, saying the special effects were the real star.
associations: Close Encounters of the Third Kind

facts.label: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
facts.statement: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial (1982) was written by Melissa Mathison, then Harrison Ford's wife; Ford's cameo was cut.

facts.label: Jurassic Park and Schindler's List
facts.statement: In 1993 Jurassic Park set a first-week box-office record while Schindler's List won Best Picture; the latter led to the USC Shoah Foundation.

facts.label: Hook
facts.statement: Hook (1991) is his Peter Pan fantasy, with Glenn Close in a cameo as a male pirate and Smee calling the title pirate "unfathomable."
